claim: Mutations in KCNQ2 cause neonatal epileptic encephalopathy, a complex disorder presenting with severe early-onset seizures and impaired neurodevelopment.
source: Mutations in KCNQ2, which encodes a pore-forming K+ channel subunit responsible for neuronal M-current, cause neonatal epileptic encephalopathy, a complex disorder presenting with severe early-onset seizures and impaired neurodevelopment.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Patient iPSC-derived neurons exhibit faster action potential repolarization.
source: We find that patient iPSC-derived neurons exhibit faster action potential repolarization, larger post-burst afterhyperpolarization and a functional enhancement of Ca2+-activated K+ channels.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Patient iPSC-derived neurons exhibit larger post-burst afterhyperpolarization.
source: We find that patient iPSC-derived neurons exhibit faster action potential repolarization, larger post-burst afterhyperpolarization and a functional enhancement of Ca2+-activated K+ channels.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Patient iPSC-derived neurons exhibit a functional enhancement of Ca2+-activated K+ channels.
source: We find that patient iPSC-derived neurons exhibit faster action potential repolarization, larger post-burst afterhyperpolarization and a functional enhancement of Ca2+-activated K+ channels.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: These properties can be recapitulated by chronic inhibition of M-current in control neurons.
source: These properties, which can be recapitulated by chronic inhibition of M-current in control neurons, facilitate a burst-suppression firing pattern that is reminiscent of the interictal electroencephalography pattern in patients.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The altered properties facilitate a burst-suppression firing pattern that is reminiscent of the interictal electroencephalography pattern in patients.
source: These properties, which can be recapitulated by chronic inhibition of M-current in control neurons, facilitate a burst-suppression firing pattern that is reminiscent of the interictal electroencephalography pattern in patients.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Dyshomeostatic mechanisms compound KCNQ2 loss-of-function leading to alterations in the neurodevelopmental trajectory of patient iPSC-derived neurons.
source: Our findings suggest that dyshomeostatic mechanisms compound KCNQ2 loss-of-function leading to alterations in the neurodevelopmental trajectory of patient iPSC-derived neurons.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the totality of experimental data.

claim: KCNQ2 and KCNQ3 proteins form heterotetrameric channels in mature neurons.
source: In mature neurons, KCNQ2 and the paralogous KCNQ3 protein form heterotetrameric channels (KCNQ2/3; Wang et al., 1998; Schwake et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KCNQ2/3 channels mediate the M-current, a slowly activating and non-inactivating voltage-dependent K+ conductance suppressed by Gq protein-coupled muscarinic acetylcholine receptor activation.
source: Together these channels mediate the M-current, a slowly activating and non-inactivating voltage-dependent K+ conductance suppressed by Gq protein-coupled muscarinic acetylcholine receptor activation (Brown and Adams, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The M-current activates as neurons approach action potential threshold and acts to dampen neuronal excitability.
source: The M-current activates as neurons approach action potential (AP) threshold and acts to dampen neuronal excitability (Brown and Adams, 1980; Brown and Passmore, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KCNQ2/3 channels help set the AP threshold and contribute to the post-burst afterhyperpolarization, which limits repetitive firing following bursts of action potentials.
source: Therefore, KCNQ2/3 channels help set the AP threshold and contribute to the post-burst afterhyperpolarization (AHP), which limits repetitive firing following bursts of action potentials (Storm, 1989; Zhang and McBain, 1995; Devaux et al., 2004; Tzingounis and Nicoll, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KCNQ2/3 channels are enriched at the axon initial segment and nodes of Ranvier, and are also expressed at lower densities at the soma, dendrites and synaptic terminals of neurons.
source: These channels are enriched at the axon initial segment (AIS) and nodes of Ranvier, and are also expressed at lower densities at the soma, dendrites and synaptic terminals of neurons (Devaux et al., 2004; Chung et al., 2006; Pan et al., 2006; Shah et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Disorders caused by KCNQ2 mutations include benign familial neonatal seizures (BFNS), characterized by seizures that remit within the first year of life.
source: Disorders caused by KCNQ2 mutations include benign familial neonatal seizures (BFNS), characterized by seizures that remit within the first year of life (Charlier et al., 1998; Singh et al., 1998) and the more severe neonatal developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE; Millichap and Cooper, 2012; Saitsu et al., 2012; Weckhuysen et al., 2012; Kato et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Disorders caused by KCNQ2 mutations include the more severe neonatal developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE).
source: Disorders caused by KCNQ2 mutations include benign familial neonatal seizures (BFNS), characterized by seizures that remit within the first year of life (Charlier et al., 1998; Singh et al., 1998) and the more severe neonatal developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE; Millichap and Cooper, 2012; Saitsu et al., 2012; Weckhuysen et al., 2012; Kato et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A search for KCNQ2 on ClinVar results in 710 different variants.
source: A search for KCNQ2 on ClinVar, which tracks genetic variation in relation to disease, results in 710 different variants, some of which are recurrent.
evidence: This is a factual statement based on a database search.

claim: Mutations in KCNQ2 account for approximately 5% of all mutations identified in genetic epilepsy.
source: Mutations in KCNQ2 account for approximately 5% of all mutations identified in genetic epilepsy (von Deimling et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017) and 10% of those associated with early-onset forms of DEE (Afawi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mutations in KCNQ2 account for 10% of those associated with early-onset forms of DEE.
source: Mutations in KCNQ2 account for approximately 5% of all mutations identified in genetic epilepsy (von Deimling et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017) and 10% of those associated with early-onset forms of DEE (Afawi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The main clinical features of DEE are developmental and cognitive disabilities, with early onset of severe seizures that occur within a few days after birth, and are often refractory to antiepileptic drug treatment.
source: The main clinical features of DEE are developmental and cognitive disabilities, with early onset of severe seizures that occur within a few days after birth, and are often refractory to antiepileptic drug treatment (Auvin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The earliest hypothesis to explain epilepsy associated with KCNQ2 mutations posited that loss of KCNQ2 channel function allows for sustained membrane depolarization after a single action potential leading to increased repetitive firing within bursts in excitatory neurons.
source: The earliest hypothesis to explain epilepsy associated with KCNQ2 mutations posited that loss of KCNQ2 channel function allows for sustained membrane depolarization after a single action potential leading to increased repetitive firing within bursts in excitatory neurons (Cooper and Jan, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Some variants associated with severe clinical phenotypes produce gain-of-function effects.
source: However, some variants associated with severe clinical phenotypes produce gain-of-function effects (Millichap et al., 2017; Mulkey et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Enhanced K+ conductance, specifically in the AIS, could hyperpolarize the AIS membrane and relieve steady state inactivation of sodium channels, which would increase the rate of action potential activation and action potential repolarization.
source: Enhanced K+ conductance, specifically in the AIS, could hyperpolarize the AIS membrane and relieve steady state inactivation of sodium channels. This would increase the rate of action potential activation and action potential repolarization (Niday and Tzingounis, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from a 13-year-old female clinically diagnosed with KCNQ2-DEE.
source: To investigate the effects of mutant KCNQ2 in human neurons, we isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from a 13-year-old female clinically diagnosed with KCNQ2-DEE.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Clinical genetic sequencing revealed a de novo heterozygous KCNQ2 variant (c.1742G>A) resulting in an arginine to glutamine missense mutation at position 581 (p.Arg581Gln, R581Q).
source: Clinical genetic sequencing revealed a de novo heterozygous KCNQ2 variant (c.1742G>A) resulting in an arginine to glutamine missense mutation at position 581 (p.Arg581Gln, R581Q; KCNQ2 splice variant 1: NM_172107.4; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the genetic variant identified in the patient, supported by Figure 1A.

claim: The arginine residue at position 581 is highly conserved across species.
source: The arginine residue is highly conserved across species, and this mutation has been observed in at least four other individuals diagnosed with KCNQ2-DEE (ClinVar variation #21769; Olson et al., 2017; Clinical Study Group et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and database information.

claim: The R581Q mutation has been observed in at least four other individuals diagnosed with KCNQ2-DEE.
source: The arginine residue is highly conserved across species, and this mutation has been observed in at least four other individuals diagnosed with KCNQ2-DEE (ClinVar variation #21769; Olson et al., 2017; Clinical Study Group et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and database information.

claim: Mutation of residue 581 to other amino acids has been reported in at least five other cases with similar pathology (R581L, R581P, and R581G).
source: Moreover, mutation of this residue to other amino acids has been reported in at least five other cases with similar pathology (R581L, R581P, and R581G; ClinVar variations #205920, #804957 and #265380, respectively), as well as in three individuals with less severe BFNS (R581Ter; ClinVar variation #21768).
evidence: This is supported by database information.

claim: Mutation of residue 581 has been reported in three individuals with less severe BFNS (R581Ter).
source: Moreover, mutation of this residue to other amino acids has been reported in at least five other cases with similar pathology (R581L, R581P, and R581G; ClinVar variations #205920, #804957 and #265380, respectively), as well as in three individuals with less severe BFNS (R581Ter; ClinVar variation #21768).
evidence: This is supported by database information.

claim: R581Q is located in a highly conserved coiled-coil domain of the C-terminus referred to as the C-helix.
source: R581Q is located in a highly conserved coiled-coil domain of the C-terminus referred to as the C-helix.
evidence: This is a description of the location of the mutation within the protein structure.

claim: Disruption of the coiled-coil domain abolishes the ability of KCNQ2 to form functional homomeric and heteromeric (KCNQ2/KCNQ3) channels and prevents transport to the plasma membrane.
source: Disruption of this coiled-coil domain abolishes the ability of KCNQ2 to form functional homomeric and heteromeric (KCNQ2/KCNQ3) channels and prevents transport to the plasma membrane (Schwake et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: R581Q alone or combined with wild-type KCNQ2 produced 81.6% and 56.6% smaller current density, respectively, as compared to cells expressing wild-type channels.
source: We found that KCNQ2-R581Q alone or combined with wildtype KCNQ2 produced 81.6% (t test: p<0.0001) and 56.6% (t test: p=0.006) smaller current density, respectively, as compared to cells expressing wild-type channels (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The findings are consistent with a KCNQ2 loss-of-function.
source: These findings are consistent with a KCNQ2 loss-of-function.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: iPSCs were derived from PBMCs using integration-free, Sendai virus-mediated reprogramming.
source: We derived iPSCs from PBMCs using integration-free, Sendai virus-mediated reprogramming.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: An isogenic mutation-corrected control iPSC line was generated from the patient-derived line using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing.
source: To create a model that would allow us to attribute any phenotypic differences to the disease-associated genetic variant, we generated an isogenic mutation-corrected control iPSC line from the patient-derived line (Figure 1C). We specifically corrected the mutant allele using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing and simultaneously introduced two silent mutations in the protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) to prevent re-cleavage (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study, supported by Figure 1C.

claim: The resulting iPSCs exhibited a normal female karyotype, typical stem cell morphology, and expressed pluripotency markers, including nuclear NANOG and the cell surface antigen SSEA4.
source: The resulting iPSCs exhibited a normal female karyotype, typical stem cell morphology, and expressed pluripotency markers, including nuclear NANOG and the cell surface antigen SSEA4 (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2D–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: No evidence for off-target edits was found in any of the top 10 predicted genomic regions with homology to the targeted KCNQ2 exon using a T7 endonuclease-based assay.
source: We found no evidence for off-target edits in any of the top 10 predicted genomic regions with homology to the targeted KCNQ2 exon using a T7 endonuclease-based assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and Supplementary file 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Whole genome sequencing confirmed the genetic correction and integrity of the targeted gene, and found that there were no edits in any of all 74 predicted off-target sites.
source: As an additional quality control, we performed whole genome sequencing (WGS) of samples Q2-04R581Q/+ (29.41x coverage) and isoQ2-04+/+ (28.12x coverage) and determined that they correspond to the same individual (pi_hat score = 0.99). We also validated the genetic correction and integrity of the targeted gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C), and found that there were no edits in any of all 74 predicted off-target sites indicating highly specific CRISPR activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, inner arrows, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C and 3B.

claim: Cortical excitatory neurons were differentiated through a modified NGN2 overexpression protocol.
source: Given the clinical presentation of KCNQ2-associated DEE and the focal source of seizures that reside in the cortex (Wilmshurst et al., 2015; Fisher et al., 2017), we chose to study cortical excitatory neurons, differentiated through a modified NGN2 overexpression protocol (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A; Zhang et al., 2013; Nehme et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used in the study, supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Over 95% of GFP-positive cells were also MAP2-positive for all iPSC lines.
source: Over 95% of GFP-positive cells were also MAP2-positive for all iPSC lines.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: All neurons that were GFP and MAP2 positive also expressed vGLUT1.
source: Furthermore, all neurons that were GFP and MAP2 positive also expressed vGLUT1 (Figure 1F,G and Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: The differentiated neuronal cultures expressed high levels of vGLUT2, FOXG1, and BRN2, which are characteristic of excitatory layer 2/3 cortical neurons.
source: As previously described (Zhang et al., 2013), we found that these cultures expressed high levels of vGLUT2, FOXG1, and BRN2, which are characteristic of excitatory layer 2/3 cortical neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 4D and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4D and citations.

claim: The differentiated neuronal cultures expressed several KCNQ2 splice variants by RT-qPCR.
source: Importantly, we confirmed that the differentiated neuronal cultures expressed several KCNQ2 splice variants by RT-qPCR (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: One of the clinical hallmarks of KCNQ2-DEE is an interictal burst-suppression pattern recorded by EEG during the first few days of life.
source: One of the clinical hallmarks of KCNQ2-DEE is an interictal burst-suppression pattern (i.e. paroxysmal bursts of activity interspersed with periods of electrical silence) recorded by EEG during the first few days of life (Weckhuysen et al., 2012; Milh et al., 2013; Millichap et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons exhibited a significantly greater number of active electrodes and slightly higher spontaneous firing frequency early in their maturation (DIV: 10-13), relative to isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: Interestingly, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons exhibited a significantly greater number of active electrodes (p<0.0001) and slightly higher spontaneous firing frequency (p=0.0081) early in their maturation (DIV: 10-13), relative to isoQ2-04+/+ neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons can fire spontaneously earlier than isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: This suggests that Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons are able to fire spontaneously earlier than isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The number of active electrodes was not different between Q2-04R581Q/+ and isoQ2-04+/+ neurons at later times in culture (DIV: 15-31).
source: However, the number of active electrodes was not different between Q2-04R581Q/+ and isoQ2-04+/+ neurons at later times in culture (DIV: 15-31) (p=0.0896; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The distribution of spiking in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons was dramatically and increasingly irregular compared to isogenic control neurons, indicated by the increased inter-spike interval coefficient of variation (ISI CoV).
source: More strikingly, the distribution of spiking in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons was dramatically and increasingly irregular compared to isogenic control neurons, indicated by the increased inter-spike interval coefficient of variation (ISI CoV; p<0.0001; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The irregularity in spiking was associated with greater bursting propensity, with short intervals between spikes in bursts and longer intervals between bursts.
source: This irregularity was associated with greater bursting propensity, with short intervals between spikes in bursts and longer intervals between bursts.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Compared to isogenic control neurons, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had increased average number of bursts detected on single electrodes.
source: Compared to isogenic control neurons, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had increased average number of bursts detected on single electrodes (repeated measures ANOVA for genotype: F(1,455) = 17.31, ***p<0.0001; genotype/day interaction: F(7,455) = 3.88, ###p=0.0004)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Compared to isogenic control neurons, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had increased number of spikes within bursts.
source: number of spikes within bursts (repeated measures ANOVA for genotype: F(1,455) = 17.31, ***p<0.0001; genotype/day interaction: F(7,455) = 2.24, #p=0.0301)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Compared to isogenic control neurons, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had increased percentage of all detected spikes which were found to occur within bursts.
source: and percentage of all detected spikes which were found to occur within bursts (repeated measures ANOVA for genotype: F(1,455) = 135.47, ***p<0.0001; genotype/day interaction: F(7,455) = 5.89, ###p<0.0001; See Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons were more prone to fire in bursts rather than single tonic spikes compared to isogenic control neurons.
source: These results indicate that Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons were more prone to fire in bursts rather than single tonic spikes compared to isogenic control neurons (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by Figure 2E.

claim: The bursting phenotype became even more pronounced and phasic over time.
source: Moreover, the significant interaction of genotype and day in culture suggest that this bursting phenotype became even more pronounced and phasic over time.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons developed significantly smaller inter-burst interval CoV only after day 22 in culture, and thus their bursts became more regular and phasic.
source: This is further supported by the fact that Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons developed significantly smaller inter-burst interval CoV only after day 22 in culture, and thus their bursts became more regular and phasic (p=0.0169; Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had a significantly more depolarized RMP and higher input resistance only during week 3.
source: However, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had a significantly more depolarized RMP (p=0.0163) and higher input resistance (p=0.0075) only during week 3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Table 1.

claim: The increasing AP amplitudes for both genotypes over the course of 5 weeks indicate some progress in functional neuronal maturation.
source: The increasing AP amplitudes for both genotypes over the course of 5 weeks indicate some progress in functional neuronal maturation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Table 1; Bardy et al., 2016; Nehme et al., 2018; Lindhout et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and citations.

claim: Compared with isoQ2-04+/+ neurons, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had slower AP repolarization with longer AP half-width at week 3.
source: We observed that compared with isoQ2-04+/+ neurons, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had slower AP repolarization with longer AP half-width at week 3 (p=0.0383; Figure 3C,D; Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, D and Table 1.

claim: Slower AP repolarization is consistent with a reduced M-current.
source: Slower AP repolarization is consistent with a reduced M-current.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data based on known properties of M-current.

claim: Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons progressively developed faster AP repolarization with shorter AP half-widths at week 5.
source: However, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons progressively developed faster AP repolarization with shorter AP half-widths at week 5 and larger fast component of the AHP (fAHP) at week 4 (p=0.03) and at week 5 (p=0.035; Figure 3C,D and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, D and Table 1.

claim: Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons had larger fast component of the AHP (fAHP) at week 4 and at week 5.
source: However, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons progressively developed faster AP repolarization with shorter AP half-widths at week 5 and larger fast component of the AHP (fAHP) at week 4 (p=0.03) and at week 5 (p=0.035; Figure 3C,D and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, D and Table 1.

claim: There was no difference in AP thresholds between Q2-04R581Q/+ and isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: There was no difference in AP thresholds.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Faster AP repolarization would enable neurons to fire a greater number of APs more rapidly with less synaptic input, which may explain the enhanced number of spikes per burst and higher tendency of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons to fire within bursts.
source: Faster AP repolarization would enable neurons to fire a greater number of APs more rapidly with less synaptic input, which may explain the enhanced number of spikes per burst and higher tendency of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons to fire within bursts (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Previous studies have shown the involvement of KCNQ2 channels in the medium AHP (mAHP) in cortical neurons.
source: Previous studies have shown the involvement of KCNQ2 channels in the medium AHP (mAHP) in cortical neurons (Guan et al., 2011; Battefeld et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Compared to controls, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons exhibited significantly larger mAHPs (peak of AHP) and slow post-burst AHPs (sAHP; 1 s after last stimulus).
source: Compared to controls, Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons exhibited significantly larger mAHPs (peak of AHP) and slow post-burst AHPs (sAHP; 1 s after last stimulus; p<0.0001 and p<0.0001, respectively; Figure 3E,F and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E, F and Table 1.

claim: Isogenic control neurons exhibited a time-dependent attenuation in the mAHP and sAHP and thus were significantly smaller than Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons during weeks 4–5 but not earlier.
source: Surprisingly, isogenic control neurons exhibited a time-dependent attenuation in the mAHP and sAHP and thus were significantly smaller than Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons during weeks 4–5 but not earlier (Figure 3E,F and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E, F and Table 1.

claim: An enhanced AHP increases the refractory latency of neurons to repolarize and fire again after a burst of APs.
source: Although an enhanced AHP increases the refractory latency of neurons to repolarize and fire again after a burst of APs, the faster repolarization observed for Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons may counterbalance this effect.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on known neurophysiological principles.

claim: The faster repolarization observed for Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons may counterbalance the effect of enhanced AHP.
source: Although an enhanced AHP increases the refractory latency of neurons to repolarize and fire again after a burst of APs, the faster repolarization observed for Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons may counterbalance this effect.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The changes in AP properties account for more APs fired within bursts, whereas enhanced post-burst AHPs dampen spontaneous firing between bursts.
source: These findings are consistent with enhanced phasic burst firing in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons. The changes in AP properties account for more APs fired within bursts, whereas enhanced post-burst AHPs dampen spontaneous firing between bursts (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by Figure 2.

claim: Previous studies have shown that blocking M-current in rodent cortical excitatory neurons acutely with XE991 enhances neuronal excitability by lowering AP threshold, impairing AP repolarization and attenuating the post-burst AHP.
source: Previous studies have shown that blocking M-current in rodent cortical excitatory neurons acutely with XE991 enhances neuronal excitability by lowering AP threshold, impairing AP repolarization and attenuating the post-burst AHP (Yue and Yaari, 2004; Santini and Porter, 2010; Lezmy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: XE991 significantly lowered AP threshold and slowed AP repolarization in control neurons.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Yue and Yaari, 2004; Santini and Porter, 2010; Lezmy et al., 2017), XE991 significantly lowered AP threshold and slowed AP repolarization (AP threshold: p=0.0104; HW: p=0.0046; fAHP: p=0.009; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-E and citations.

claim: XE991 blunted the mAHP and sAHP amplitudes in control neurons.
source: Furthermore, XE991 blunted the mAHP and sAHP amplitudes in these neurons (mAHP: p=0.0014; sAHP: p=0.022; Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: The effects of acute XE991 treatment did not resemble the behavior of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons, suggesting that loss of M-current alone is not sufficient for phasic burst firing.
source: These effects did not resemble the behavior of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons, suggesting that loss of M-current alone is not sufficient for phasic burst firing.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: KCNQ2-DEE neurons develop a more pronounced phasic bursting phenotype progressively as a result of chronic M-current reduction coupled with dyshomeostatic adaptation of intrinsic membrane properties at different temporal scales.
source: Collectively, these experiments suggest that KCNQ2-DEE neurons develop a more pronounced phasic bursting phenotype progressively as a result of chronic M-current reduction coupled with dyshomeostatic adaptation of intrinsic membrane properties at different temporal scales.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of this section, based on the totality of experimental data.

claim: Strong candidates for dyshomeostatic mechanisms are large, intermediate, and small conductance, Ca2+- and voltage-gated BK (KCNMA1) and IK/SK (KCNN4/KCNN1-3) channels that participate in fast AP repolarization and slow Ca2+-dependent post-burst AHP, respectively.
source: While a number of different channels might contribute to a dyshomeostatic mechanism, strong candidates are large, intermediate, and small conductance, Ca2+- and voltage-gated BK (KCNMA1) and IK/SK (KCNN4/KCNN1-3) channels that participate in fast AP repolarization and slow Ca2+-dependent post-burst AHP, respectively (Storm, 1990; Iyer et al., 2017; Latorre et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: On week 3, KCNMA1 (BK channel), KCNN4 (IK channel), and KCNA4 (encoding KV1.4 channel) expression was higher in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons.
source: By contrast, KCNMA1 (BK channel), KCNN4 (IK channel), and KCNA4 (encoding KV1.4 channel) expression was higher in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons (p=0.0429, p=0.016 and p=0.0216, respectively; Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: By week 5, the difference in KCNMA1, KCNN4 and KCNA4 was no longer significant but other differences had emerged, including an upregulation of KCNMB3, KCNN1, KCNN2, KCNA1, and KCNA2, and downregulation of KCNQ5 expression in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons relative to controls.
source: By week 5, the difference in KCNMA1, KCNN4 and KCNA4 was no longer significant but other differences had emerged, including an upregulation of KCNMB3, KCNN1, KCNN2, KCNA1, and KCNA2, and downregulation of KCNQ5 expression in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons relative to controls (p=0.0081, p<0.0001, p=0.018, p=0.0099, p=0.0017 and p=0.0198, respectively; Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: These genes, which encode a BK channel β-subunit, SK channels (SK1 and SK2), KV1.1 and KV1.2, respectively, have been implicated in epilepsy and developmental delay in human and animal studies.
source: These genes, which encode a BK channel β-subunit, SK channels (SK1 and SK2), KV1.1 and KV1.2, respectively, have been implicated in epilepsy and developmental delay in human and animal studies (Hu et al., 2003; Lorenz et al., 2007; McKay et al., 2012; Lerche et al., 2013; Masnada et al., 2017; Paulhus et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The upregulation of KCNMB3, KCNN1, KCNN2, KCNA1, and KCNA2 is consistent with a gain of a K+ conductance suggested by electrophysiological studies.
source: and their upregulation is consistent with a gain of a K+ conductance suggested by our electrophysiological studies (i.e. BK/SK upregulation can lead to larger post-burst AHPs and BK/KV1.1/KV1.2 upregulation can lead to faster AP repolarization).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Addition of apamin reduced the mAHP in both Q2-04R581Q/+ and isoQ2-04+/+ neurons, and reduced the sAHP only in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons.
source: Addition of apamin (500 nM), a SK channel antagonist, reduced the mAHP in both groups, and reduced the sAHP only in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The magnitudes of change of the mAHP and sAHP were significantly larger for Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons compared to isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: The magnitudes of change of the mAHP (ΔmAHP: p=0.0001) and sAHP (ΔsAHP: p<0.0001) were significantly larger for Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons compared to isoQ2-04+/+ neurons (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: Functional enhancement of SK channels in KCNQ2-DEE neurons contributes to the increase of slowly deactivating Ca2+-activated currents that determine the level of post-burst AHP.
source: These data suggest that functional enhancement of SK channels in KCNQ2-DEE neurons contributes to the increase of slowly deactivating Ca2+-activated currents that determine the level of post-burst AHP.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Blocking SK and BK channels reduced the ISI CoV of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons to the level observed in untreated controls.
source: Blocking SK and BK channels reduced the ISI CoV of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons (p=0.0015) to the level observed in untreated controls, while treatment did not affect isoQ2-04+/+ neurons (p=0.796; Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Addition of apamin and paxilline had a significantly larger effect on the number of spikes/burst and burst % in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons than in isogenic control neurons.
source: Addition of both drugs also had a significantly larger effect on the number of spikes/burst (ΔSpikes/Burst: p=0.0087) and burst % (ΔBurst%: p=0.0254) in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons than in isogenic control neurons.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Pharmacological treatment with apamin and paxilline specifically reduced the bursting features to the levels seen in isogenic control neurons before drug application.
source: This pharmacological treatment specifically reduced the bursting features to the levels seen in isogenic control neurons before drug application (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Inhibition of SK and BK channels in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons reduces post-burst AHPs and normalizes phasic burst firing behavior.
source: Together, these data suggest that inhibition of SK and BK channels in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons reduces post-burst AHPs and normalizes phasic burst firing behavior.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Chronically XE991-treated control neurons exhibited enhanced repolarization and larger post-burst AHPs relative to untreated controls.
source: Chronically XE991-treated control neurons exhibited enhanced repolarization (half width: p=0.0002; fAHP: p=0.01) and larger post-burst AHPs (mAHP: p=0.0001; sAHP: p=0.0008) relative to untreated controls (Figure 6B–E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B and Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B-E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B and Table 2.

claim: The effects of chronic XE991 treatment were identical to or larger than the properties observed for untreated Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons.
source: Importantly, these effects were identical to or larger than the properties observed for untreated Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Chronic XE991 treatment effectively phenocopied the electrophysiological behavior of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: This experimental paradigm effectively phenocopied the electrophysiological behavior of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons and suggests that the enhanced AP repolarization and larger post-burst AHP that we identified in KCNQ2-DEE neurons, occur as a result of long-term reduction of M-current.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The enhanced AP repolarization and larger post-burst AHP identified in KCNQ2-DEE neurons occur as a result of long-term reduction of M-current.
source: This experimental paradigm effectively phenocopied the electrophysiological behavior of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons and suggests that the enhanced AP repolarization and larger post-burst AHP that we identified in KCNQ2-DEE neurons, occur as a result of long-term reduction of M-current.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Within 24 hr of adding XE991 to the neuronal media, there was an increase in the number of active electrodes approximately three times higher in XE991-treated relative to untreated isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: Within 24 hr of adding XE991 to the neuronal media (DIV: 12-13), we observed an increase in the number of active electrodes approximately three times higher in XE991-treated relative to untreated isoQ2-04+/+ neurons (p<0.0001; Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and C.

claim: Within 24 hr of adding XE991, there was a sevenfold increase in burst % in XE991-treated isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: This was accompanied by a sevenfold increase in burst % (p<0.0001; Figure 6—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: The magnitude of change in mean firing frequency on active electrodes was not significantly affected by XE991 in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons.
source: However, the magnitude of change in mean firing frequency on active electrodes was not significantly affected by XE991 in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons (p=0.4557; Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: XE991 induced a relatively fast upregulation of spontaneously firing isoQ2-04+/+ neurons to the levels of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons.
source: Thus, XE991 induced a relatively fast upregulation of spontaneously firing isoQ2-04+/+ neurons to the levels of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Chronic M-current inhibition led to long-term enhanced burst firing parameters such as ISI CoV, number of bursting electrodes and bursts, number of spikes per burst and burst %.
source: Furthermore, chronic M-current inhibition led to long-term enhanced burst firing parameters such as ISI CoV, number of bursting electrodes and bursts, number of spikes per burst and burst % (p<0.0001, p=0.0011, p=0.0275, p<0.0001, p<0.0001, respectively; Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The effects of chronic M-current inhibition on bursting in control neurons were more dramatic than the inherent bursting phenotype in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons, likely because of the less severe loss of function associated with the mutation relative to the pharmacological treatment with XE991.
source: The effects of chronic M-current inhibition on bursting in control neurons were more dramatic than the inherent bursting phenotype in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons, likely because of the less severe loss of function associated with the mutation relative to the pharmacological treatment with XE991 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by Figure 1B.

claim: Expression of KCNMA1, KCNMB3, KCNN1, KCNN2, KCNN4, KCNA1, and HCN1 was significantly higher in chronically XE991-treated isogenic control neurons compared to untreated neurons at week 5.
source: Expression of KCNMA1, KCNMB3, KCNN1, KCNN2, KCNN4, KCNA1, and HCN1 was significantly higher in chronically XE991-treated isogenic control neurons compared to untreated neurons (p=0.0038, p=0.0148, p=0.0179, p=0.0307, p=0.0175, p=0.0443, and p=0.0002, respectively; Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Acute application of paxilline and apamin on MEAs during week 5 restored the bursting behavior of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons and chronically XE991-treated isogenic control neurons to the levels of untreated control neurons.
source: Lastly, acute application of paxilline and apamin on MEAs during week 5, restored the bursting behavior of Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons and chronically XE991-treated isogenic control neurons to the levels of untreated control neurons (Figure 5 and Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 and Figure 6—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Upregulation of SK and BK channel function exacerbates bursting in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons, and is a result of reduced M-current.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that upregulation of SK and BK channel function exacerbates bursting in Q2-04R581Q/+ neurons, and is a result of reduced M-current.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Neurons derived from an iPSC line heterozygous for a loss-of-function KCNQ2 mutation exhibited progressive escalation of burst firing and developed intrinsic membrane properties that promoted phasic bursting as they matured over time in culture.
source: Our study demonstrated that neurons derived from an iPSC line heterozygous for a loss-of-function KCNQ2 mutation exhibited progressive escalation of burst firing and developed intrinsic membrane properties that promoted phasic bursting as they matured over time in culture.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: The altered pattern of neuronal firing featured properties not previously associated with loss of M-current (faster AP repolarization and enhanced AHP).
source: This altered pattern of neuronal firing featured properties not previously associated with loss of M-current (faster AP repolarization and enhanced AHP).
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: KCNQ2 dysfunction induces dyshomeostatic plasticity and alters the neurodevelopmental trajectory of KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
source: Our findings suggest that KCNQ2 dysfunction induces dyshomeostatic plasticity and alters the neurodevelopmental trajectory of KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Repeated firing in bursts of high-frequency action potentials has been associated with chronic epilepsy both in experimental models and in humans.
source: Repeated firing in bursts of high-frequency action potentials has been associated with chronic epilepsy both in experimental models and in humans (Sanabria et al., 2001; Schindler et al., 2006; Gast et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KCNQ2-DEE neurons became active earlier and were more prone to fire in bursts rather than single tonic spikes exhibited by isogenic control neurons.
source: Our analysis of firing patterns using MEAs indicated that KCNQ2-DEE neurons became active earlier and were more prone to fire in bursts rather than single tonic spikes exhibited by isogenic control neurons.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: As KCNQ2-DEE neurons matured, their bursts became increasingly pronounced with more spikes/burst and more phasic or regularly distributed intervals.
source: As KCNQ2-DEE neurons matured, their bursts became increasingly pronounced with more spikes/burst and more phasic or regularly distributed intervals.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The combination of increased post-burst AHP and the later onset of enhanced AP repolarization in single neurons results in increased number of spikes per burst and longer refractory periods between bursts.
source: This is supported by the combination of increased post-burst AHP and the later onset of enhanced AP repolarization in single neurons, which results in increased number of spikes per burst and longer refractory periods between bursts.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The burst-suppression firing pattern is reminiscent of the interictal EEG pattern observed in KCNQ2-DEE patients.
source: This burst-suppression firing pattern is reminiscent of the interictal EEG pattern observed in KCNQ2-DEE patients (Steriade, 2004; Timofeev and Steriade, 2004; Weckhuysen et al., 2012; Millichap et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by citations.

claim: This type of activity does not necessarily reflect more neuronal APs, but rather an alteration in the neuronal discharge pattern (i.e. bursts rather than irregular single spikes) and propensity of KCNQ2-DEE neurons to fire within bursts.
source: Importantly, this type of activity does not necessarily reflect more neuronal APs, but rather an alteration in the neuronal discharge pattern (i.e. bursts rather than irregular single spikes) and propensity of KCNQ2-DEE neurons to fire within bursts.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Neurons dynamically adjust the expression and function of ion channels as well as the structure of their processes to regulate intrinsic excitability in response to cell autonomous defects or the environment.
source: Neurons dynamically adjust the expression and function of ion channels as well as the structure of their processes to regulate intrinsic excitability in response to cell autonomous defects or the environment.
evidence: This is a statement of general knowledge in the field.

claim: During chronically induced hyperexcitability, neurons downscale their intrinsic excitability and alter the size and location of the AIS.
source: For example, during chronically induced hyperexcitability, neurons downscale their intrinsic excitability and alter the size and location of the AIS (Turrigiano and Nelson, 2004; Grubb and Burrone, 2010; Wolfart and Laker, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pyramidal neurons in heterozygous knock-in mice harboring the loss-of-function pathogenic T274M variant exhibited hyperexcitability early on (P7-P9), but this effect went away in later life (P28-35).
source: Interestingly, Biba et al., recently reported that pyramidal neurons in heterozygous knock-in mice harboring the loss-of-function pathogenic T274M variant, exhibited hyperexcitability early on (P7-P9), but this effect went away in later life (P28-35; Biba et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Homeostatic changes also take place in neurons in vivo as a consequence of mutant KCNQ2.
source: While the involvement of other channels, or the AHP specifically, were not examined, these results suggest that homeostatic changes also take place in neurons in vivo as a consequence of mutant KCNQ2 .
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings from a previous study.

claim: M-current inhibition with XE991 acutely increased the firing rate of cultured hippocampal pyramidal neurons but chronic XE991 treatment restored firing to baseline levels.
source: Furthermore, Lezmy et al. reported that M-current inhibition with XE991 acutely increased the firing rate of cultured hippocampal pyramidal neurons but chronic XE991 treatment restored firing to baseline levels.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In cultured GABAergic interneurons, XE991 treatment caused a persistent hyperexcitability that was not attenuated over time.
source: By contrast in cultured GABAergic interneurons, XE991 treatment caused a persistent hyperexcitability that was not attenuated over time (Lezmy et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Homeostatic adaptive responses may be cell type specific.
source: This suggests that homeostatic adaptive responses may be cell type specific.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings from a previous study.

claim: Selective deletion of M-channels (Kv7.2/Kv7.3) in parvalbumin GABAergic interneurons leads to their hyperexcitability and enhanced excitatory transmission in pyramidal neurons.
source: Importantly, a recent study showed that selective deletion of M-channels (Kv7.2/Kv7.3) in parvalbumin GABAergic interneurons leads to their hyperexcitability and enhanced excitatory transmission in pyramidal neurons (Soh et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Homeostatic plasticity can become maladaptive and even pathogenic, when these processes become dysfunctional.
source: Homeostatic plasticity can become maladaptive and even pathogenic, when these processes become dysfunctional (Moulder et al., 2003; Turrigiano and Nelson, 2004; Wu et al., 2008; Miranda et al., 2013; Swann and Rho, 2014; Wolfart and Laker, 2015; Wefelmeyer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The 'acquired channelopathy' hypothesis suggests that proepileptic ion channel dysfunction develops during or after the onset of epilepsy or excitotoxicity.
source: On the other hand, the 'acquired channelopathy' hypothesis suggests that proepileptic ion channel dysfunction develops during or after the onset of epilepsy or excitotoxicity (Bernard et al., 2004; Poolos and Johnston, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Fast upregulation of BK channels and associated potassium currents occurs in cortical neurons of mice after picrotoxin-induced seizure pre-sensitization.
source: For example, fast upregulation of BK channels and associated potassium currents occurs in cortical neurons of mice after picrotoxin-induced seizure pre-sensitization (Shruti et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The findings are concordant with previous work describing homeostatic responses to chronic M-current inhibition.
source: Our findings are concordant with previous work describing homeostatic responses to chronic M-current inhibition and provide further insight into the mechanisms that mediate this adaptive response by the upregulation of other ion conductances including BK and SK channels (Okada et al., 2003; Lezmy et al., 2017; Lezmy et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Suppression of M-current leads to rearrangement of neuronal intrinsic properties on different temporal scales.
source: We demonstrated that suppression of M-current leads to rearrangement of neuronal intrinsic properties on different temporal scales (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Inhibition of M-current by application of XE991 increases the number of spontaneously active neurons and their ability to fire in bursts within 24 hr.
source: Inhibition of M-current by application of XE991 increases the number of spontaneously active neurons and their ability to fire in bursts within 24 hr (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The magnitude of change in firing frequency of control neurons after a 24 hr treatment with XE991 was not significantly different from untreated neurons, while the change in % of spikes that occur within bursts was dramatically enhanced.
source: Interestingly, the magnitude of change in firing frequency of control neurons after a 24 hr treatment with XE991 was not significantly different from untreated neurons, while the change in % of spikes that occur within bursts was dramatically enhanced.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The finding that burst firing is progressively and dramatically increased in KCNQ2-DEE neurons signifies a necessity to shift how we examine neuronal disease phenotypes and focus on the pattern rather than abundance of activity.
source: Thus, our finding that burst firing is progressively and dramatically increased in KCNQ2-DEE neurons signifies a necessity to shift how we examine neuronal disease phenotypes and focus on the pattern rather than abundance of activity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: A greater number of active neurons during early time points could be directly related to the loss of M-current, which induces fast homeostatic rearrangement of intrinsic properties to upregulate post-burst AHPs and limit neuronal firing, as well as much slower dyshomeostatic enhancement of AP repolarization.
source: A greater number of active neurons during early time points could be directly related to the loss of M-current, which induces fast homeostatic rearrangement of intrinsic properties to upregulate post-burst AHPs and limit neuronal firing, as well as much slower dyshomeostatic enhancement of AP repolarization (by weeks 4 and 5).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: KCNQ2-DEE neurons, examined at week 3, exhibited some properties consistent with a loss of M-current (i.e. hyperpolarized RMP, increased IR, longer AP half-widths and a trend for smaller fAHPs) and associated with a bursting phenotype.
source: KCNQ2-DEE neurons, examined at week 3, exhibited some properties consistent with a loss of M-current (i.e. hyperpolarized RMP, increased IR, longer AP half-widths and a trend for smaller fAHPs; Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B) and associated with a bursting phenotype.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Soon after week 3, KCNQ2-DEE neurons developed shorter AP half-widths and larger fAHPs associated with increased spikes/burst, as well as regularity of burst firing.
source: However, soon after (week 4 and beyond) KCNQ2-DEE neurons developed shorter AP half-widths and larger fAHPs associated with increased spikes/burst, as well as regularity of burst firing.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: This suggests a maladaptive upregulation of fast voltage-gated K+ conductances over time.
source: This suggests a maladaptive upregulation of fast voltage-gated K+ conductances over time.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The upregulation in KCNMB3 expression in KCNQ2-DEE neurons partially explains the increased AP repolarization as β3 subunits transform BK channels to be fast-inactivating.
source: Accordingly, the upregulation in KCNMB3 expression in KCNQ2-DEE neurons partially explains the increased AP repolarization as β3 subunits transform BK channels to be fast-inactivating (Storm, 1989; Xia et al., 1999; Hu et al., 2003; Zeng et al., 2007; Kaufmann et al., 2010; Li and Yan, 2016; Latorre et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by citations.

claim: The upregulation of KCNA1 and KCNA2 is also consistent with enhanced AP repolarization.
source: The upregulation of KCNA1 and KCNA2 is also consistent with enhanced AP repolarization (Colasante et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data, supported by a citation.

claim: Chronic M-current inhibition in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons enhanced the expression of KCNMA1, KCNMB3 and KCNA1 which could explain why AP repolarization in these neurons is even faster than in KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
source: Chronic M-current inhibition in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons enhanced the expression of KCNMA1, KCNMB3 and KCNA1 which could explain why AP repolarization in these neurons is even faster than in KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The magnitude of the mAHP and sAHP did not change over time in KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
source: Conversely, the magnitude of the mAHP and sAHP did not change over time in KCNQ2-DEE neurons, suggesting that either the driver for post-burst AHPs is upregulated early and fails to be developmentally downregulated (as the AHP in isoQ2-04+/+ neurons becomes smaller at week 4; Figure 3E,F), or there are multiple mechanisms through which the AHP is enhanced.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 3E and F.

claim: Activation of Ca2+-activated K+ channels underlies the medium and slow AHP.
source: Activation of Ca2+-activated K+ channels underlies the medium and slow AHP (Lancaster and Adams, 1986; Zhang and McBain, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Enhanced, apamin-sensitive upregulation of post-burst AHPs in KCNQ2-DEE neurons correlated with increased KCNN1 and KCNN2 gene expression at week 5.
source: We observed enhanced, apamin-sensitive upregulation of post-burst AHPs in KCNQ2-DEE neurons, which correlated with increased KCNN1 and KCNN2 gene expression at week 5.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings.

claim: The magnitude of the post-burst AHP is positively related to the rise of intracellular Ca2+ that accumulates with repeated AP firing.
source: The magnitude of the post-burst AHP is positively related to the rise of intracellular Ca2+ that accumulates with repeated AP firing.
evidence: This is a statement of general knowledge in the field.

claim: Higher frequency and longer duration of activity leads to greater influx and accumulation of intracellular Ca2+.
source: Higher frequency and longer duration of activity leads to greater influx and accumulation of intracellular Ca2+ (for review, see Storm, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous review.

claim: A combination of increased SK channel expression and activity-dependent Ca2+ accumulation contribute to the enhanced AHP in KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
source: As KCNQ2-DEE neurons exhibit more spikes/burst, it is also likely that a combination of increased SK channel expression and activity-dependent Ca2+ accumulation contribute to the enhanced AHP in KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Higher expression of KCNMA1 and KCNN4 at week 3 but not week 5 suggests multiple developmentally regulated molecular mechanisms that drive post-burst AHPs.
source: Furthermore, higher expression of KCNMA1 and KCNN4 (encoding an apamin-insensitive IK channel) at week 3 but not week 5 suggests multiple developmentally regulated molecular mechanisms that drive post-burst AHPs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: BK channel α-subunit alone does not inactivate and thus can participate in the post-burst AHP.
source: BK channel α-subunit alone does not inactivate and thus can participate in the post-burst AHP (Storm, 1989; Xia et al., 1999; Kaufmann et al., 2010; Li and Yan, 2016; Latorre et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Chronic XE991 treatment increased expression of KCNMA1, KCNN1, KCNN2, and KCNN4 at week 5 suggesting that stronger suppression of M-current may exacerbate dyshomeostatic upregulation of these channels.
source: Moreover, chronic XE991 treatment increased expression of KCNMA1, KCNN1, KCNN2, and KCNN4 at week 5 suggesting that stronger suppression of M-current may exacerbate dyshomeostatic upregulation of these channels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: SK2 (KCNN2) overexpression or activation impairs cognitive function and learning and memory.
source: Interestingly, SK2 (KCNN2) overexpression or activation impairs cognitive function and learning and memory (Hammond et al., 2006; McKay et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Both SK and BK channels contribute to the increased K+ conductance that enhances AP repolarization as well as AHPs, and leads to phasic bursting in KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
source: Our experiments with apamin and paxilline suggest that both SK and BK channels contribute to the increased K+ conductance that enhances AP repolarization as well as AHPs, and leads to phasic bursting in KCNQ2-DEE neurons.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Increased K+ conductance may not be traditionally associated with hyperexcitability and epilepsy, but several studies have shown that inhibition of K+ conductances improves learning and memory in wild-type mice, or seizure susceptibility in a model of Angelman syndrome.
source: Although, increased K+ conductance may not be traditionally associated with hyperexcitability and epilepsy, several studies have shown that inhibition of K+ conductances improves learning and memory in wild-type mice, or seizure susceptibility in a model of Angelman syndrome (Stackman et al., 2002; Fontán-Lozano et al., 2011; Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Gain-of-function mutations in several K+ channels including KCNQ2, KCNQ3, KCNQ5, BK, SK3, KCNT1, and KV4.2 have been reported in genetic epilepsy and developmental disorders.
source: Furthermore, gain-of-function mutations in several K+ channels including KCNQ2, KCNQ3, KCNQ5, BK, SK3, KCNT1, and KV4.2 have been reported in genetic epilepsy and developmental disorders (Niday and Tzingounis, 2018; Bauer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Targeting the underlying cause of KCNQ2-DEE might not be effective if started late in the disease course.
source: Because KCNQ2-DEE patients present with seizures in the first days of life, targeting the underlying cause might not be effective if started late in the disease course.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the clinical presentation of the disease.

claim: Targeting dyshomeostatically altered ion currents might offer an alternative therapeutic strategy for the cognitive and developmental deficits in KCNQ2-DEE.
source: Our study suggests that targeting dyshomeostatically altered ion currents might offer an alternative therapeutic strategy for the cognitive and developmental deficits in KCNQ2-DEE.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The iPSC-based platform developed may be valuable to identify effective therapeutics and address further questions regarding the spatiotemporal mechanisms of DEE due to KCNQ2 mutations.
source: The iPSC-based platform we developed may be valuable to identify effective therapeutics and address further questions regarding the spatiotemporal mechanisms of DEE due to KCNQ2 mutations.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of the study.
